races.title: State House, District 70
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brian Biggs
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House for District 70 (parts of Randolph County) since January 2023. A real estate broker for over 20 years, he served on the Randolph County Board of Education from 2014 to 2022. He beat incumbent Pat Hurley in the 2022 primary.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Brian Biggs was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. We found no documented actions or stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site says only that he supports religious freedom, property rights and the military, and it gives no specific policy positions. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2022, 2024 or 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any of those years. We found no news reports of controversies about him. The Ballotpedia page's sponsored-legislation list was empty in the copy we read, so we could not confirm which bills he sponsored.

qual.background: Has served in the NC House since 2023 and was elected House Deputy Majority Whip, per his campaign site. Served on the Randolph County Board of Education 2014-2022, including four years as vice-chair. Has been a commercial and residential real estate broker for over 20 years.
qual.why: Scored in the upper-middle range because he has prior legislative service and eight years of local elected office, plus a long business career. No law, policy or budget career outside the legislature was found. Committee seats and chairs were not counted.

cands.name: William (Bill) McCaskill
cands.bio: Retired Child Protective Services supervisor from Asheboro with a 32-year career in child welfare. Graduated from East Carolina University in 1972. Says he is a former Asheboro City Council member. Ran for NC House District 78 in 2016 and District 70 in 2026, both as a Democrat.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to North Carolina. His Asheboro City Council service is stated only on his campaign site, with no dates and no council votes found. We found no record of his role on the state child-welfare committee beyond his own description. We found no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership by investors or foreigners, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, campaign donor policy, policing, guns, or abortion. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Beyond his 2016 and 2026 candidacies, no record of public office actions was found.

qual.background: Worked 32 years in Child Protective Services, including 25 years on the front lines and 7 as a supervisor. His campaign site says he served on the Asheboro City Council, which Ballotpedia does not confirm. He ran unsuccessfully for the NC House in 2016.
qual.why: A supervisory career in a public agency plus claimed local elected office puts him in the middle band. No state legislative service or budget or law career is shown. The state child-welfare committee, the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council chair role and board seats add nothing under the rubric.
